channel.title: Cadence Evidence — PT Research Signal
channel.description: Daily curated physical therapy & rehab research for clinicians. AI-scored signal from 56 sources.

item.title: Can traditional Chinese exercises help people with musculoskeletal disorders? - BJSM blog - social media's leading SEM voice
item.description: An umbrella review of 92 meta-analyses of RCTs found high-certainty evidence that traditional Chinese exercises improved physical function and mental health in knee osteoarthritis, mental health in neck pain, and sleep quality in fibromyalgia, with Tai Chi showing the most consistent benefits.
item.author: BJSM

item.title: Diagnosis, Rehabilitation, and Return to Sport after Athletic Hamstring Injury: An ICCUS Society Consensus Statement.
item.description: An ICCUS Society expert consensus statement, developed via a modified Delphi process with 17 clinicians, achieved over 80% agreement on 54 statements concerning athletic hamstring injury management, emphasizing standardized classification, individualized criterion-based rehabilitation, progressive loading, and multi-faceted return-to-sport criteria.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Gait variability as a predictor of fall risk in patients with stroke: A 6-month prospective cohort study with survival analysis.
item.description: In a 6-month prospective cohort study of 112 stroke patients, stride time variability (STV) at discharge, with an optimal cutoff of 3.40% (AUC 0.756, sensitivity 88.2%, specificity 53.8%), was identified as the sole independent predictor of post-discharge falls, outperforming conventional measures.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effects of Exercise Type and Duration on Pain, Function, and Quality of Life in Patients With Knee Osteoarthritis: A Systematic Review With Bayesian Network Meta-Analysis.
item.description: A systematic review with Bayesian network meta-analysis of 35 trials (n = 3808) found short-term combined aerobic and resistance exercise had the largest effect on pain (SMD = -0.937), function (SMD = -0.590), and quality of life (SMD = 0.663) in patients with knee OA.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Immediate task-specific and delayed generalized adaptations to variable dual-task training in community-dwelling older adults: a randomized waitlist-controlled trial
item.description: A 12-week variable dual-task training program for older adults (n=50) led to immediate gains in functional lower-limb strength (5xSTS: SMD = 0.54) and delayed improvements in functional mobility, inhibitory control, and short-term memory at 3-month follow-up.
item.author: BMC Geriatrics

item.title: Interval Between Injury and Surgery Influences Knee Biomechanics During Walking in Anterior Cruciate Ligament Reconstructed Patients: A Systematic Review with Meta-analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 16 studies (18-55 years) found ACLR patients have lower peak knee flexion angle (SMD = -0.33), peak knee adduction angle (SMD = -0.47), and peak knee flexion moment (SMD = -0.64) during walking. Delayed reconstruction (≥ 12 months) is associated with persistent sagittal plane deficits, while early surgery (< 6 months) is linked to fewer long-term sagittal-plane deficits but temporary frontal-plane asymmetries and extension deficits.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Comparative Effects of Neurostimulation- and Technology-Augmented Robot-Assisted Training on Upper-Limb Motor Recovery After Stroke: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-Analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and network meta-analysis of 103 trials (N = 5,251) found rTMS plus robot-assisted training (RAT) yielded the largest FMA-UE estimate (MD 9.56 points), followed by LFES plus RAT (MD 7.52) compared to usual care, with RAT alone showing smaller gains (MD 3.83).
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Neurocognitive Factors in ACL Injury: The Missing Piece in Rehabilitation and Prevention? A Scoping Review.
item.description: A scoping review of 42 studies identified neurocognitive factors, particularly dual-task interference and visual attention, as significant missing components in ACL injury rehabilitation and prevention. It suggests integrating neurocognitive challenges into rehabilitation and return-to-sport testing to better identify secondary injury risk.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Comparative Efficacy of Low-Level Laser Therapy in Patients With Carpal Tunnel Syndrome: An Updated Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
item.description: An updated systematic review and meta-analysis of 16 RCTs found low-level laser therapy (LLLT) significantly reduced pain (Hedges' g=-1.524, P <0.001) and improved grip strength (Hedges' g=0.391, P=0.002) in carpal tunnel syndrome. Pulsed mode was superior for analgesia, continuous for grip strength.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effects of chair-based exercise training on pulmonary function, exercise capacity, and quality of life in patients with acute exacerbation of COPD: A randomised controlled trial.
item.description: A randomized controlled trial (n=30) found that chair-based exercise training in patients hospitalized with acute COPD exacerbations significantly improved functional exercise capacity (mean 6MWT distance change 50.9 m [95% CI 2.09-99.76]; p=0.042), dyspnea, and quality of life compared to breathing exercises alone.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effectiveness of wearable and non-wearable biofeedback on knee biomechanics during functional tasks in anterior cruciate ligament injury prevention and rehabilitation: a systematic review and meta-analysis
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis found that biofeedback interventions significantly reduced peak knee abduction angle (Hedges’ g = 0.52, 95% CI 0.06 to 0.98) in ACL injury prevention, but the certainty of evidence was low to very low, with no significant effects on other knee biomechanics.
item.author: BMC Sports Sci Med Rehabil

item.title: Feasibility, Safety, and Preliminary Effect Estimates of an Ultrasound-Informed Hybrid Joint-Sparing Rehabilitation Strategy in Patients With Rheumatoid Arthritis: A Prospective Non-Randomized Proof-of-Concept Study.
item.description: A 12-week ultrasound-informed hybrid rehabilitation protocol for rheumatoid arthritis was found feasible and safe in 60 patients, showing greater pain reduction (ΔVAS: -2.88 cm vs. -0.60 cm; p < 0.001) than a control group, though effect sizes may be overestimated and specific ultrasound attribution was limited.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Walking Capacity and Daily Movement Behaviours After Ischemic Stroke: A Potential Capacity-Performance Gap.
item.description: A cross-sectional study of ambulatory ischemic stroke patients found a capacity-performance gap: participants accumulated ~12 hours/day of sedentary time despite walking speeds approaching community ambulation, with gait speed being the only walking capacity measure associated with daily movement behaviors.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Healthcare professionals' perceptions and experiences of promoting physical activity in persons with multiple sclerosis: a systematic review of qualitative evidence.
item.description: A systematic review of eight qualitative studies identified healthcare professional-based, organizational, social, and patient-related factors influencing physical activity promotion in persons with multiple sclerosis. Findings suggest improving promotion requires MS-specific education for professionals, practical resources, and stronger cross-sector coordination.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Adherence System Usability Patient Experience and Psychosocial Impact in Robot Assisted Gait Neurorehabilitation A Cross Sectional Study.
item.description: This observational study of 250 adults in robot-assisted gait neurorehabilitation found that greater attendance, system usability, and rehabilitation experience were associated with favorable psychosocial impact (r s = 0.41 to 0.53, all p < 0.001). This association remained significant after adjusting for diagnosis, age, sex, and disease duration.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Gamified Versus Traditional Balance Training: Effects on Balance and Motivation in Collegiate Student-Athletes.
item.description: In this quasi-experimental controlled trial, 30 collegiate athletes (19.8 ± 0.9 years) were pseudo-randomized to gamified (Wii Fit, n=9), traditional (wobble board, n=11) balance training, or control (n=10). Both training groups showed significant improvements in mSEBT anterior reach (+6.5 cm) and composite scores (+21.6 cm for gamified, +18.5 cm for traditional) compared to control (p < 0.01). Gamified training yielded higher IMI interest/enjoyment scores (5.0 ± 1.2 vs. 3.2 ± 1.3; p < 0.01, d = 1.50).
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Comparison of Radiofrequency Microtenotomy vs. Heavy-Slow Resistance for Refractory Plantar Fasciopathy: A Randomised Controlled Trial
item.description: A randomized controlled trial (n=72) found no significant difference in FHSQ-DK pain domain mean change from baseline to 6 months between radiofrequency microtenotomy and heavy-slow resistance training for refractory plantar fasciopathy (mean difference −4.9, 95% CI −13.8; 4.0).
item.author: Sports Med - Open

item.title: Radiographic quantification of active self-correction during physiotherapeutic scoliosis-specific exercises and its potential prognostic value in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis
item.description: A prospective study (n=not specified) found that active self-correction during physiotherapeutic scoliosis-specific exercises (PSSE) resulted in 27.32% Cobb angle correction (from 37.57° to 28.82°) and was the only variable significantly associated with 6-month post-treatment Cobb angle change.
item.author: BMC Musculoskelet Disord

item.title: Physical and psychosocial outcomes in children with limb loss 2-years after the 2023 Kahramanmaras-Türkiye earthquakes
item.description: A retrospective analysis (n=56) of children with earthquake-related limb loss 2.3 years post-amputation showed favorable physical, social, and school-related quality of life (median PedsQL 72.3/100.0), but lower emotional functioning (60.0/100.0). Unilateral lower limb loss was associated with superior adjustment and prosthetic satisfaction.
item.author: medRxiv

item.title: Effectiveness of a Structured Post-Platelet Rich Plasma Rehabilitation Approach on Pain and Function in Subacromial Pain Syndrome: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
item.description: A 21-day structured post-PRP rehabilitation approach, added to standard physiotherapy, significantly improved pain (VAS: 9.00 ± 0.67 to 2.92 ± 1.14 vs. 9.11 ± 0.64 to 7.96 ± 0.75, p < 0.001) and function in 27 subacromial pain syndrome participants compared to standard physiotherapy alone.
item.author: PubMed
